headline: Hasan Mahmud takes 6 wickets to bowl out Australia for 198 in Darwin
summary: Bangladesh is in the driving seat on Day 1 of the first Test, trailing by only 102 runs with 9 wickets in hand.
details: Bangladesh's fast bowlers dominated the opening day of the first Test against Australia at Marrara Stadium in Darwin, bowling out the hosts for 198.
Hasan Mahmud delivered a career-best performance, claiming 6 for 55. He became the first Bangladeshi bowler to take a Test five-wicket haul on Australian soil.
Steve Smith was the only significant threat for Australia, scoring 71 runs. However, he admitted after the match that he had nicked a delivery from Ebadot Hossain that was not given out by the DRS.
Despite Smith's resistance, the Tigers' bowling attack remained relentless, with Hasan Mahmud eventually dismissing Smith in the third session.
At stumps on Day 1, Bangladesh is 96 for 1 in their first innings, trailing by 102 runs and comfortably positioned to take a lead.
The match continues tomorrow with Bangladesh looking to build on their strong start to the series.
caption:
A historic day for the Tigers! Hasan Mahmud claims a career-best 6-wicket haul to dismantle Australia in their own backyard.

Bangladesh's fast bowlers dominated the opening day of the first Test against Australia at Marrara Stadium in Darwin, bowling out the hosts for 198.

Hasan Mahmud delivered a career-best performance, claiming 6 for 55. He became the first Bangladeshi bowler to take a Test five-wicket haul on Australian soil.

Steve Smith was the only significant threat for Australia, scoring 71 runs. However, he admitted after the match that he had nicked a delivery from Ebadot Hossain that was not given out by the DRS.

Despite Smith's resistance, the Tigers' bowling attack remained relentless, with Hasan Mahmud eventually dismissing Smith in the third session.

At stumps on Day 1, Bangladesh is 96 for 1 in their first innings, trailing by 102 runs and comfortably positioned to take a lead.

The match continues tomorrow with Bangladesh looking to build on their strong start to the series.

headline: 693 hospitalised in 24 hours as 2 more die of dengue
summary: The national death toll has risen to 65 with 22,243 total cases recorded across Bangladesh.
details: At least two dengue patients died and 693 others were hospitalised across Bangladesh in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00 am today, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The two reported deaths occurred in areas under the two Dhaka city corporations.
With these new fatalities and cases, the total number of dengue deaths in the country has risen to 65, while the total number of cases has reached 22,243.
Currently, 1,615 dengue patients are receiving treatment at hospitals nationwide.
caption:
